findings.F1: Inside the falling agitated profile, the fade belongs to the largest rises only. On the non-overlapping 3-day grid, in-profile rises split into terciles of the scaled 3-day rise give these unusual 3-day moves: small +0.22 % (t 0.15, 38 days), mid +0.16 % (t 0.10, 35 days), large −3.24 % (t −1.88, 29 days). The book's mean forecast was −2.1, −6.4 and −14.9 in the three terciles, so a third of its short exposure sat on rises that gave nothing back.
findings.F2: On in-profile rises, the least-squares slope of the unusual 3-day move on the scaled 3-day rise is −0.0184 (t −2.19, 180 cases on 75 days). The slope is −0.0069 on in-profile falls (t −0.47) and +0.0052 out of the profile (t 2.10, 397 days). The grading of the theme's effect exists, but only on the rise side.
findings.F3: The in-profile slope is at or below zero in all 7 windows with enough cases: w13, w14, w16, w17 and w18 negative, w9 and w15 at +0.0002. The window with the most cases, w18, gives −0.0275 (t −1.43, 22 days).
findings.F4: Across all in-profile grid bars, the 3-day quintiles fall from +3.08 % after the largest falls (t 1.27) to −2.94 % after the largest rises (t −1.83, 29 days). The Spearman correlation of the scaled 3-day rise with the next 3-day move is −0.167 in the profile (p 0.001, n 427) against +0.069 outside it (p 0.001, n 2261). The sign flip between profiles is what the brief claims.
findings.F5: The book earns only when the largest rises fade. On its best 5 % of active coin-days the coin fell 7.6 % on average, and on its worst 5 % it rose 9.8 %. Its mean daily return on days in a position is 0.0048 % against the 0.05 % required, because the many small-rise shorts add cost and nothing else.
findings.F6: The 1-day patterns inside the profile repeat ideas the map already holds, so none is a discovery. The largest 1-day falls are followed by +2.14 % the next day (t 2.89, 116 days), the same as the held "falling agitated daily fall rebound" ideas (047-01, 051-01). The other angles show nothing beyond chance given how many were looked at: weekday (no 1-day weekday |t| above 1.3), own-volatility tercile (|t| ≤ 1.06) and close location (|t| ≤ 1.18).

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's 3-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days is followed by a fall over the next 3 days that grows faster than the rise itself. The largest rises against usual swing give back several percent, and ordinary rises give back almost nothing.
ideas.consequence: In an agitated decline, a trader would short only the rallies that stand far out against usual swing, sizing the short steeply with their extremity, rather than fading every few-day rise.
ideas.name: extreme rally fade falling agitated
